financial_infrastructure.sector: Indian financial-market infrastructure and household savings formalization
financial_infrastructure.headline: CAMS is a credible long-term compounder candidate. Current price requires successful execution rather than merely continued adoption.

current_price.source: Official NSE CM bhavcopy retained by parent

financial_infrastructure.structural_thesis: More organized financial saving increases balances, repeat transactions and recordkeeping. CAMS can spread compliance and technology costs over an established AMC base, while payments, KRA and alternatives add profitable adjacent revenue.
financial_infrastructure.counter_thesis: Market appreciation is not net saving, and higher AUM is not equal revenue growth. Fee yield erodes with telescopic pricing, passive mix and negotiation. Technology spending, weak markets and capital allocation can prevent per-share cash from compounding as the theme grows.
financial_infrastructure.company_selection_rationale: Largest incumbent MF platform in the comparison, recurring asset-linked revenue, cash-funded core and currently lower indicative profit multiple than KFin or CDSL. This is not a claim that it dominates every forward scenario.
financial_infrastructure.current_price_judgment: At INR724.65, a favorable INR400cr starting cash normalization needs 13.28% company cash growth for ten years for a 10% illustrative investor return at 25x terminal cash. Plausible at the favorable end of current evidence, not established. Strong structural priority and conditional buy potential, without a demonstrated broad valuation margin.

cash_normalization.interpretation: Zero working-capital change is a diagnostic. It removes timing noise without erasing technology investment. Sustained growth must still fund working capital.

growth_feasibility.judgment: Plausible at the favorable end, with insufficient evidence to treat the full path as already underwritten.
growth_feasibility.bridge_needed: Cash growth must exceed roughly 10–12% revenue growth via productivity, maturing capex and profitable adjacent-business mix. Initial headcount reductions and non-MF margins support that possibility. Old and new technology run together and project-level realized ROIC is not disclosed.

reverse_valuation.cash_rules: All future cash is assumed after required reinvestment and distributed annually. No accumulated cash is added again. Opening treasury credited once. No universal hurdle.

capital_allocation.fy26_newer_businesses: Fintuple, Think Analytics India, account aggregation and insurance repository remained loss-making. Aggregate high ROE is not proof of project-level incremental returns.
capital_allocation.share_claims: One-to-five split effective 2025-12-05. September issued shares 248418378 after 433880 H1 option shares. No H1 new grants. Exact November share count is not independently verified.

financial_infrastructure.management_controls: Audited profitable record, explicit current pricing discussion and measurable early productivity. FY26 audit notes backup-location/timing exception for one subsidiary with two step-down subsidiaries, backups from 2025-05-15. No detected edit-log tampering reported. Integrity not certified by this bounded review.

historical_failure_mechanisms.mechanism: Financial-crisis aftereffects and entry-load abolition produced sluggish AUM and required business-model adjustment despite low long-term penetration.
FY23 parent PAT declined slightly and FY26 grew about 1.2%, so secular adoption does not ensure smooth annual profit growth.

limitations: Current issued share count is verified to 30 September, not independently to 20 November. A 0.5% annual dilution allowance is an assumption.
Reported CFO includes SBC add-back. Share dilution is modeled instead of also deducting the same SBC amount as cash. No future option exercise proceeds are credited.
Zero working-capital movement is a diagnostic, not a sustainable funded-growth assumption.
All PPE and software capex is retained. Acquisitions and joint venture investments are separate capital-allocation uses, not included in recurring selected cash.
INR650cr treasury credit is provisional. It is below INR875.10cr gross treasury and allows for the already-earned dividend, buffers and other claims. It is not an audited free-cash number.
Annual future cash is assumed distributable only after all future reinvestment and taxes. Growth feasibility is not established by this reverse calculation.
Opening treasury is credited once. All modeled annual owner cash is distributed and is not added again to terminal cash.
Lease payments are deducted annually. The entire lease liability is not also subtracted from opening equity value.
Terminal multiple, discount rate and growth assumptions are sensitivities, not forecasts or a universal hurdle.
Rolling rounded reported EPS sums are approximate because weighted share counts can differ between periods.
This is not a blind point-in-time replay or a demonstrated source of alpha.
KFin and CDSL receive a bounded comparison, not full funded valuation. NSDL price is not inferred.

power.name: APAR Industries
power.review_scope: Completed bounded structural/financial case and conditional reverse valuation. Not a fully funded forecast or approved capital deployment.
power.structural_thesis: Grid capacity, reconductoring, specialized cables and transformer-fluid demand can reward qualification, field execution and product capability over a decade. Customer and partner records establish actual capability before the present cycle.
power.strongest_counter_thesis: Premiumization and international demand could make current high unit economics more durable, so a normalized profit base near INR1800cr and 20% long-term growth could make the current price attractive. That requires funded per-share growth, not extrapolation of metal prices or temporary oil spreads.
power.current_price_judgment: PASS_CURRENT_PRICE for a new five-year position. Maintain a ten-year structural case with observable operating and price conditions. Not an all-market cash view.
power.scenario_assumptions: Working case: INR1400cr assumed normalized starting PAT, 15% annual PAT growth, 25x exit, 20% payout and 0.3% annual dilution. The prior INR1200cr/8%/20x row is preserved as lower_growth. A separate profit_reset sensitivity starts from reported FY26 PAT of INR976.93cr with 8% growth and 20x exit, using the same payout and dilution. FY26 is an observable stress anchor, not an asserted sustainable normal. Gross nominal INR returns include assumed dividends and exclude personal tax and trading costs. Additional external equity funding is not modeled.

comparators.name: Power Grid Corporation of India
comparators.structural_thesis: Commission and operate essential transmission capacity, funded over a long asset life.
comparators.strongest_counter_thesis: Most new work is competitive TBCB. Weak bid tariffs, cost overruns, commissioning delays or higher financing costs can reduce returns despite high investment.
comparators.current_price_judgment: Priority structural alternative at more moderate earnings valuation. Bounded comparator, not a completed BUY case.

key_metrics.caution: Reported rounded per-share inputs, no modeled project returns, dividend-payment confirmation or full capital-change sweep.

comparators.name: GE Vernova T&D India
comparators.structural_thesis: Qualified high-voltage systems, complex execution and a global manufacturing network.
comparators.strongest_counter_thesis: Current equipment margins and valuation can normalize as capacity and competition expand, with related-party exposure and contract risk.
comparators.current_price_judgment: Strong operating business, no purchase conclusion from bounded review.

review_correction.change: Renamed original downside case lower_growth and added a distinct profit-reset sensitivity.
review_correction.reason: The former downside starting PAT of INR1200cr already exceeded FY26 actual of INR976.93cr and did not capture a reset to that observed profit level.
review_correction.scope: Conditional sensitivity, no change to historical facts, normalized-profit uncertainty, working case, probabilities or current-price disposition.

health.structural_thesis: Ageing, chronic monitoring and organized diagnosis can sustain demand. Dense integrated regional networks may capture value through trusted access, equipment utilization and direct consumer collection.
health.counter_thesis: Growing need attracts supply and stronger organized payers. New clusters may fail to earn the core region's cash returns. A 79.5x TTM earnings multiple already requires a long period of strong per-share compounding.
health.current_price_judgment: Business quality is supported, funding appears manageable, but a current buy is not established. A 15% EPS path over ten years produces only 4.3–7.4% price CAGR at 30–40x exit. 20% EPS growth gives 8.9–12.0%. These are unprobabilized reverse sensitivities, not funded forecasts or total-return IRRs.
